subject: Governance: smoke checklist, rollforward plan & network gating for private deployment
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 07:30:00 +0000
Subject: Private deployment: last-mile gating and smoke run window

Hi Olga / Markus,

Thanks for getting us this far. We have the 08:00–10:00 UTC window on June 8th reserved for the on-prem switch. Before we flip traffic we need a concise checklist we can run with our SREs and a clear rollforward plan if anything degrades. Specific asks: 

- Final smoke checklist that includes network ACL verification (east/west + public egress), KMS access from the customer side, and quick end-to-end inference validation.
- Expected propagation delay for firewall/ACL changes (we need a conservative SLA).
- A one-page rollforward (and rollback) decision tree for the first 2 hours after go-live.
- A signed contact list for escalation (phone + slack) in case we need immediate coordination.

Can you send the checklist and the plan by EOD today so we can circulate to Acme infra? Attached is our internal change request ticket for context.

Attachments: acme-cr-9876.pdf (we did not attach it here; reference only)

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Platform Lead — Acme Logistics
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:05:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: last-mile gating and smoke run window

Jordan — thanks. Draft attached: "smoke-checklist-v1.xlsx" and a short "rollforward-playbook.pdf". High-level plan below; full checklist is in the spreadsheet (see link and attachment).

Planned verification sequence (order matters):
1) Infrastructure gating: confirm VPN/DirectConnect + BGP peers up.
2) Network ACLs: application subnets allow control-plane range + outbound to KMS endpoints.
3) KMS test: decrypt a test token using customer-managed key (we will run under their credentials).
4) SSO/OIDC: complete an ID token exchange and ensure session propagation to the private control plane.
5) Runtime smoke: run 10 concurrent small requests (<=64 tokens) and validate latency p95 and success rate.
6) Observability sanity: confirm traces, token-level billing markers, and error logs are visible in Console.

Rollforward/rollback guidance (summary):
- If ACL change fails or KMS errors (>30% request failures) => immediate rollback to previous static routing, fail traffic to Hosted-tier (policy-based fallback).
- If tracing/observability is degraded but traffic OK => continue and open a hotfix with priority P1.

I'll coordinate a quick 20-min sync at 16:00 UTC today to walk through the checklist; invite will follow.

Attachments: smoke-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), rollforward-playbook.pdf

—
Olga Petrov
Manager, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +44 20 5555 0150
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:02:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: last-mile gating and smoke run window

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 09:05 Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Planned verification sequence (order matters):
> 1) Infrastructure gating: confirm VPN/DirectConnect + BGP peers up.
> 2) Network ACLs: application subnets allow control-plane range + outbound to KMS endpoints.

Adding technical specifics from infra:
- BGP LLGR: we see potential route flaps when we apply the AS-path prepend; recommend a 5-minute stabilization window post-change before running traffic tests.
- Firewall/NAT mapping: Acme must allow source NAT from our edge IP range (listed in sheet). If they put a stateful timeout < 60s for UDP flows, the KV-cache warmup may fail – call this out in the runbook.
- Expected ACL propagation: 60–120s for cloud-managed firewalls, 3–7 minutes for on-prem devices (depending on vendor). We should plan for the worst-case for the first run.

I attached a short diff of the ACL changes we will request (network-acl-diff.txt). We'll coordinate with Vivek on exact timing.

-Markus
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:18:02 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: last-mile gating and smoke run window

Markus / Olga — quick notes from Network Ops: 
- I can be on the change with Acme's infra team at 08:00 UTC on June 8th.
- Firewall rule push will take ~5 minutes in our template lab, but as Markus said we should expect up to 7 minutes on some CPE. Plan to wait 10 minutes before starting runtime smoke tests.
- Probing: we will run L3 ping and TCP handshake probes from three vantage points (edge1/edge2/customer-gw) and record RTT and packet loss.
- Warmup: we'll pre-warm KV caches with a small batch of synthetic requests 15 minutes prior to cut. That will reduce the cold-start noise.

I'll update the spreadsheet with exact IPs and proposed timestamps.

—Vivek
Senior Network SRE
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:43:30 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: last-mile gating and smoke run window

Thanks all — a couple of last clarifications from Acme: 
- KMS: we will provide a test DEK and a read-only IAM role by 17:00 UTC today. Please confirm the exact API call sequence you need so our infra can whitelist it.
- SSO: we need a pre-flight token exchange example (curl or SDK) so we can validate our OIDC federation during the 15-minute warmup.
- Escalation list: please include a phone number for after-hours (we have a standby pager group).

Can you also confirm that if we see >30% errors in the first 10 minutes, your automated routing policy will fail traffic to Hosted-tier and keep us on the previous static route? We need that in writing for our change review board.

Jordan
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: last-mile gating and smoke run window

Jordan — final confirmations below and action items for tomorrow (go-live window 08:00–10:00 UTC, Tue Jun 8).

Confirmation summary:
- KMS sequence: we will perform a DecryptRequest against the customer DEK using the provided read-only role. Exact sequence and sample curl is in the Drive link: https://redwood.app/drive/1a2b3c-smoke-checklist (sheet tab: KMS-tests).
- SSO/OIDC: sample token exchange script is included in the sheet (tab: SSO). Please validate before 18:00 UTC; we'll need a green pass to proceed.
- Failover guarantee: yes — automated routing policy will route to Hosted-tier only if the traffic-level policy sees <30% failed requests and p95 latency within agreed SLO. If >30% errors during the first 10 minutes, we will fail traffic back to the prior static route and execute the rollforward-playbook.pdf rollback branch. We will capture a signed entry in change control once actioned.

Action items (owners):
- Acme: deliver test DEK + read-only role (by 17:00 UTC today) — Jordan / infra-team
- Olga: publish final spreadsheet and meeting invite (done) — Olga
- Vivek: push ACL diff and probes; update timestamps in sheet (by 16:00 UTC) — Vivek
- Markus: pre-authorize the route rollback commands with ops (by EOD) — Markus
- Hannah: collect escalation phone list and confirm pager policy (by 17:30 UTC) — Hannah

Attachments included in thread: smoke-checklist-v1.xlsx, network-acl-diff.txt, rollforward-playbook.pdf

Please reply here with a short "ACK" when you have the DEK and the SSO test validated.

Thanks — looking forward to a clean run.

—

Manager, Deployment Engineering | Redwood Inference
